AINA Research & Assurance Programme

AINA is a deterministic authority-enforcement architecture that treats probabilistic AI outputs as untrusted proposals. It independently validates evidence, authorization, execution identity, and permitted state transitions at the boundary where external effects are committed, producing independently verifiable evidence when an attempted operation is refused.

1. The Specific Security Problem: Why Probabilistic Guardrails Cannot Govern Consequence

As autonomous AI systems gain direct access to operating systems, databases, code execution, and cyber-physical actuators, four structural failure gaps emerge at the boundary between a model's output and an external state mutation:

  1. Untrusted Proposals & Model-Monitor Failure Modes: Prompt instructions, RLHF, and secondary LLM-as-judge monitors operate over probabilistic token sequences. AINA deliberately does not rely on proving the general internal safety or alignment of an opaque neural network; instead, it restricts which externally observable operations can be authorized and checks the admissibility conditions for those operations inside a minimal, deterministic Trusted Computing Base (TCB).
  2. Multi-Agent Sycophancy & Echo-Chamber Quorum Laundering: Multiple agent instances can converge on a hallucinated or adversarial action without independent primary-source evidence.
  3. Approval-to-Execution (TOCTOU) Substitution: Between asynchronous human or policy approval and actual OS process execution, command-line arguments, environment blocks, target files, or inherited kernel handles can be substituted.
  4. Stale-Worker Overwrites & Unverifiable Rollbacks: Delayed workers holding expired clock-based TTL locks can overwrite newer state upon waking, and ordinary application logs rarely provide cryptographic proof that a refused attempt left the target resource untouched.

2. The Authority-to-Effect (A2E) Architecture & Three Enforcement Layers

AINA interposes a deterministic reference monitor at the commit boundary across four composable mechanisms and three explicit enforcement layers:

  • Evidence Instruction Set Architecture (EISA — Seven Closed Opcodes): Every proposed action must compile into a closed 10-key envelope (squad.eisa.act_envelope.v1.json) restricted to seven closed opcodes across four acyclic layers: BindEvidenceTag (Layer 0, Fracture), RequestHumanReview (Layer 0, Fracture), RejectUnlawfulAct (Layer 0, Fracture), AssertLayoutRelation (Layer 0, Forge), AssertDuplicatePair (Layer 1, Fracture), AssertTransitiveClosure (Layer 2, Fracture), and ProposePartition (Layer 3, Fracture).
  • Three Explicit Enforcement Layers:
    1. Layer 1 (Pre-Parse & Deserializer Boundary): Enforces byte caps (MAX_SUBMISSION_BYTES = 1,048,576, MAX_REQUESTED_ACT_BYTES = 65,536, MAX_EVIDENCE_REF_BYTES = 4,096), MAX_ACTS = 256, single-stage submission homogeneity, duplicate JSON key rejection (visit_map), and non-finite number rejection (visit_f64) before AST allocation.
    2. Layer 2 (Recursive Draft-07 JSON Schema Validation): Enforces recursive additionalProperties: false closure across all 12 schemas, allOf opcode-to-stage-to-operands binding, integer-only confidence basis points (0..10000, zero floats), 15 non-inferential evidence tags, 47 registered fault codes, RFC 6901 pointer depth MAX_POINTER_DEPTH = 8 (regex ^(?:/(?:[^/~\u0000-\u001f]|~[01])*){1,8}$) and MAX_POINTER_BYTES = 256, MAX_REASON_CHARS = 1,024, MAX_ID_CHARS = 64, MAX_REFS = 16, MAX_LIST = 1,000, and MAX_CHAIN = 4.
    3. Layer 3 (Runtime Four-Gate Verdict Machine & OS Kernel Confinement): Enforces MAX_CASE_BYTES = 4,194,304, MAX_CASE_RECORDS = 1,000, MAX_VALUE_CHARS = 1,024, and MIN_PHONE_DIGITS = 7 over sealed eisacase_<32hex> substrates; acyclic Layer 0 → 3 DAG resolution; counterevidence_suppressed scanning; Disjoint-Set Union-Find partition verification; and Windows NT kernel process/handle confinement.
  • Server-Cut Provenance (srv_/ev_) & Sycophancy Collapse (consensusIdentity): Requires controller-computed SHA-256 digests and exact 64-bit integer byte-offset spans (squad.evidence_ref.v1.json) prior to admission, collapsing correlated agent claims lacking independent source spans.
  • Approval-to-Execution Act-Pinning (act-pin) & Monotonic Lease Fencing: Binds a controller-fixed RequestedAct digest to the OS worker process instance across spawn and enforces monotonic integer generation fencing at commit time.
  • Proof-Carrying Non-Action (PCNA): Emits canonical JSON refusal receipts binding the refusal fault code to pre-attempt and post-refusal SHA-256 digests of the measured target resource.

4. Publicly Reproducible Evidence & Exact Claim Ceiling

Anyone can verify the public evidence bundle offline in under 10 seconds with Python 3 and zero external dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/SquadForge/blayne.aina.git
cd blayne.aina
python3 proof/verify_refusal_proof.py

What verify_refusal_proof.py proves today (Three-Part Offline Verification): (1) Manifest Integrity: All 39 published files match their SHA-256 digests in SHA256SUMS.txt; (2) Fixture & Conformance Consistency: The 3 fixture-backed refusal records (evidence-selector.json, unleased-write.json, act-pinning.json) match the exact SHA-256 digests and byte lengths of the preserved static fixtures in proof/refusal/fixtures/, stale-generation.json records an absent preimage, and the 45/45 conformance and 20/20 evidence manifests match candidate attestation; and (3) Recursive Schema & Pre-Parse Bound Validation: All 12 public JSON schemas pass recursive additionalProperties: false closure plus 18/18 positive and 26/26 negative Draft-07 and pre-parse bound tests across all 7 EISA opcodes. What it does not claim by itself: It does not by itself prove independent third-party execution of the private squad.exe binary or verify an asymmetric hardware signature authenticating receipt origin—capabilities explicitly scoped under Authenticated PCNA v2 and our independent external security audit milestone (PRJ-LC-01).

Technical Peer Review & Scoped Evaluation (§09): Bring One Real Boundary

Do not rely on a vision deck. Bring one consequential transition—workflow standing, hostile document adjudication, or protected entity resolution—or propose an independent research evaluation. We establish a written acceptance boundary, run the existing implementation, and make the positive, refusal, and unresolved evidence inspectable.
